newsitem.title: FRANCE: U.N. approves more France-Iraq wheat deals.
newsitem.headline: U.N. approves more France-Iraq wheat deals.

text.p: The U.N. has now approved the sale of a total of 400,000 tonnes of French soft wheat to Iraq under a U.N. monitored oil-for-food pact, a French government source said on Monday.
The last count on April 4 showed the total at 325,000 tonnes.
The latest approvals were given by U.N. authorities on April 28, the source said.
Traders have sold a total of 625,000 tonnes of French wheat to Iraq since December, when Iraq started selling oil to raise money for humanitarian supplies.
The source said France has also asked the U.N. to clear the sale of the remaining 225,000 tonnes of wheat.
Under a U.N. resolution easing the sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, Baghdad is allowed to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy food and medicine.
Each contract must be approved by the U.N. before the supplies can be delivered.
